kind: re-check of two explanatory notes corrected after the first verification
method: Downloaded both primary sources afresh on 2026-09-24 and compared them with the repository files. PFAS NEMP 3.0: the dcceew.gov.au host timed out after 60 seconds, so the pinned Wayback capture of the official file was used (10,682,963 bytes, SHA-256 abcc5c28177e2a96747e292e991ae46dd3d8a0099b3ca80e1750192411ce196e, the same file the corpus manifest records; PDF metadata: title 'PFAS National Environmental Management Plan version 3.0', author 'Heads of EPA Australia and New Zealand', created 3 March 2025). ASC NEPM Schedule B1: downloaded directly from legislation.gov.au (2,615,692 bytes, SHA-256 17788fb3339c5163139dc72cf67234b2276de9115d272ae7770f36c4bd77ad99, footer 'Federal Register of Legislative Instruments F2013C00288'). Text was extracted with pdfplumber and the table pages were also rendered to images and read by eye to confirm footnote markers and superscripts. Quotes below are copied from the extracted text and checked against the rendered page; line breaks are joined with a space. The server wording was read from src/evidenceline/server.py, and core.lookup_limit was run for PFOS, PFHxS and PFOS+PFHxS under 'nemp-3.0' to see what the tool actually returns. This pass did not read the other re-check or the earlier pass files. It is an automated check, not a review by a practitioner.

server_wording.text: "nemp-3.0" (PFAS NEMP 3.0, named as adopted on the WA government page) screens the SUM of PFOS and PFHxS, and PFOS alone and PFHxS alone, against 0.07 ug/L (Table 4, footnote a).
server_wording.reason: Names all three quantities the footnote names and cites the right table and footnote. The capital letters on SUM put more weight on the sum than the footnote does, but the meaning is the same. The next sentence, about the 'current' rule having no sum, is about NEMP 3.1 and was not checked here.

server_wording.text: Under 'nemp-3.0', 0.07 ug/L applies to PFOS alone, PFHxS alone and their sum (Table 4, footnote a): asking for either returns that value, with the footnote quoted.
server_wording.reason: Matches the footnote. Run on 2026-09-24, lookup_limit('PFOS', 'nemp-3.0') and lookup_limit('PFHxS', 'nemp-3.0') both return 0.07 ug/L with a caveat quoting the footnote's words "PFOS only, PFHxS only, and the sum of the two". Only that part of the footnote is quoted, not the whole sentence; that is accurate. 'either' means PFOS or PFHxS, which is clear from the context.

server_wording.id: core.lookup_limit returned fields (related, not owned here)
server_wording.text: For analyte 'PFOS' (and 'PFHxS') under 'nemp-3.0' the result has applies_to 'sum' and compared_quantity 'sum of PFOS and PFHxS'. The docstring says the result tells you 'whether it applies to the analyte on its own or to the sum of PFOS and PFHxS'.
server_wording.reason: Under footnote a the value applies to PFOS on its own as well as to the sum. When the caller asked about PFOS, a field that says the compared quantity is the sum points a reader or a model at the sum only, while the note and caveat in the same result say PFOS alone counts too. The note text is right; these two structured fields lag behind it. Suggested change for the owner of core.py (line 129) and models.py: for a member lookup under a rule whose sum value also applies to each member, set compared_quantity to the member on its own, for example 'PFOS on its own (the same value also applies to PFHxS on its own and to the sum)', and either add a third applies_to value such as 'each and sum' or reword the docstring so it no longer promises an either/or answer.

summary: Both corrected notes now match their sources: the NEMP 3.0 note says what Table 4 footnote a says, and the arsenic note matches the Table 1A(1) row label and note 2. The server instructions and the lookup_limit docstring say the same as the footnote. One related issue outside the notes: lookup_limit still labels the compared quantity as the sum when asked about PFOS or PFHxS alone under NEMP 3.0. The NEMP 3.1 half of the soil PFOS and PFHxS note was not checked.
